summary: At the run boundary, with all obligations disposed and no pending work, this step closes the last gap that could be closed by reading alone. Submission is a feedback-only research product (no map version; cites the existing S-peersjson material). Mapped: ReadPeersJSON reads a file, decodes a JSON list of address strings, maps each to a Voter whose ID equals its address, and rejects the result through checkConfiguration before returning (peersjson.go 18-45); ReadConfigJSON decodes the new-style entry list with id, address and non_voter, maps non_voter to the Nonvoter suffrage and everything else to Voter, and applies the same checkConfiguration gate (peersjson.go 48-110). So neither reader can return a configuration that later fails checkConfiguration through this path: empty IDs or addresses, duplicate IDs or addresses, and a voter-less configuration are all rejected with an error before the caller sees a Configuration, which is exactly what the previous feedback had left open. No new item was opened. The remaining frontier is now only work that needs execution or a non-crash-stop history rather than further source reading: the composed store-failure-plus-compaction history argued by reading but never executed as a single witness, the installSnapshot non-monotonic compaction variant reasoned but not exercised, the malformed-entry panic lead (DecodeConfiguration and prepareLog's default, with no recover anywhere) having no execution witness and sitting outside the crash-stop fault model, and the transport reading that described behaviour without evaluating it for defects. The run's confirmed results are unchanged: three confirmed in-scope violations (truncation-failure watermark, installSnapshot stale watermark, snapshot-trigger underflow) and one reviewed bounded no-violation (configuration rollback), against map v4. Preflight validation returns valid with no diagnostics.
